customSkills.name: Subjective POV & Scale Cropping
customSkills.triggerHint: Applies whenever any Macro-State uses subjective/POV framing or tight CU/ECU camera recalls.
customSkills.body:
Subjective POV & Framing Discipline:
- POV Subject-Camera Identity: When [CAM] or [CAM ##] specifies `POV` or `Subjective`, the camera IS the subject's eyes/head. In [ACT], direct ONLY optical displacement, world parallax, and lens-edge foreground framing (e.g., whiskers, paws, or hands intruding at the bottom frame edges).
- Never place the POV subject in third-person or lateral screen-space crossing (`darts screen-right`, `nudging his flank`, `glances up`, `scampers out`). Translate [LOGIC] forward progression into Z-axis camera surge, tilt, or banking toward/past targets.
- Tight-CU Recall Cropping: When recalling an established tight close-up (`tight CU`, `ECU`, or height-locked setup like `paw height`), verify every trait in [ACT] (upright tail, collar, overhead props) actually fits inside that tight framing; otherwise recall a wider slot or keep [ACT] strictly inside the tight frame.

customSkills.name: Montage Continuity & Duration Budget
customSkills.triggerHint: Applies when switching between montage and continuous coverage, or when Macro-State counts compete with target runtime.
customSkills.body:
Montage Independence & Duration Calibration:
- Do Not Collapse Montage into Real-Time Coverage: When a user asks for a `montage` AND asks for `continuity between shots`, preserve visual/thematic match-cuts and character appearance continuity across plain unnumbered `[CAM]` setups—do NOT silently convert back to numbered `multi_camera_coverage` (`CAM 01`–`CAM 04`) or pack unrelated gags onto one continuous block.
- Conflicting User Constraints (Beats vs. Duration): Every cut needs ~1.5s–2.5s (`max cuts = Duration(s) / 2.0`), and each Macro-State needs room for its chained `[ACT]` beats. If a user asks for more Macro-States or gags than the stated `[INTENT]` runtime can physically hold (e.g., 7 multi-action shots in 10 seconds), explicitly resolve the conflict—either consolidate cuts, keep each montage shot to one crisp single-action gag, or propose expanding the `[INTENT]` runtime (and note the tradeoff in your reply).

state_cam_visibility.instructionsOverride: Does {{STATE_ID}} describe a visual [ACT] detail (such as eyes, pupils, upright tail, collar, overhead props, or hidden hand action) that is physically hidden, unreadable, or cropped out from {{STATE_ID}}'s active [CAM] framing and shot scale?
state_cam_visibility.trueDescriptionOverride: {{STATE_ID}} describes physical or anatomical details that cannot be seen because the active camera is behind the subject, aimed elsewhere, too wide, or too tight (e.g., a tight CU/ECU or paw/hand-height setup cropping out upper-body, collar, or upright-tail action).

doc_intent_shotlist.trueDescriptionOverride: [INTENT] enumerates an ordered shot-by-shot breakdown or sequential play-by-play choreography (e.g., 'first X, then cut to Y, then Z'), rather than summarizing a multi-camera setup at a high level.

customRules.label: Subjective POV Optics Purity
customRules.instructions: If {{STATE_ID}} uses a subjective or first-person POV camera, does any [ACT] Sub-State break POV by describing the camera-holder in third person or moving laterally across the frame (e.g., 'darts screen-right', 'nudging his flank', 'glances up') instead of optical lens motion?
customRules.trueDescription: {{STATE_ID}} uses a subjective/POV camera while [ACT] describes the POV subject from outside in third person or crossing laterally screen-left/screen-right.
customRules.falseDescription: Either {{STATE_ID}} is not a subjective POV shot, or its [ACT] Sub-States strictly describe optical lens motion, world parallax, and foreground lens-edge framing.
customRules.escalationHint: Rewrite POV [ACT] Sub-States in {{STATE_ID}} purely from what the lens sees (surge, bank, tilt, foreground edge framing), removing third-person body choreography and lateral screen-direction.

customRules.label: Cut-Latency & Action Density Budget
customRules.instructions: Does [EXECUTION] exceed the target duration stated in [INTENT] by having more camera cuts than Duration(s) / 2.0, or by packing multiple sequential physical actions into individual Macro-States that leave under 1.5s per shot?
customRules.trueDescription: The scene packs too many camera cuts (exceeding Duration/2) or too many multi-step physical actions per Macro-State for the runtime declared in [INTENT].
customRules.falseDescription: Cut count stays within Duration/2 (~1.5s–2.5s per cut) and each Macro-State's choreography fits comfortably within the [INTENT] runtime.
customRules.escalationHint: Either hold/merge camera slots to stay within Duration/2 cuts, trim multi-step action cramming, or adjust [INTENT] duration to match the choreography.
